extraction.title: Add comprehensive email validation for blocked users
extraction.head: blocked-email-validation-post

greptile.text: Summarizes the PR as adding a BlockedEmail model, an EmailValidator class, and client-side tracking of rejected emails. Confidence score: 1/5 and flags ReDoS risk in EmailValidator, race conditions in BlockedEmail.should_block?, and whitelist/blacklist logic that prevents both from working together.
Style: missing space after comma in method call parameters.
Style: use modern RSpec expect syntax for the action_type default check (suggests expect(...).to eq(BlockedEmail.actions[:block])).
Logic: the custom matcher be_within_one_second_of is not defined; suggests be_within(1.second).of(Time.zone.now) instead.
Style: use modern RSpec syntax, expect(subject).to be_falsey, instead of subject.should be_false.
Style: use modern RSpec syntax, expect(subject).to be_truthy, instead of the should-based it block.
Style: use && instead of 'and' in the blocked-email condition to avoid Ruby operator precedence issues.
Logic: BlockedEmail.should_block? updates match statistics during a read-only check, causing possible race conditions and a misleading method name.
Style: use find_by(email: email) instead of where(email: email).first for idiomatic and possibly better-performing lookup.
Logic: incrementing match_count and saving separately should use increment! or a transaction to prevent races under concurrent requests.
Style: the generic 'invalid' message for rejected emails may confuse users; a more specific 'blocked' message may be clearer.

additions.text: logic: Using `elsif` means whitelist and blacklist are never applied together, which may not be intended for security restrictions.
logic: Regex `@(#{domains})` matches domain suffixes, not full domains, so `evil.example.com` would match whitelist entry `example.com`. Suggests adding `$` anchor.
logic: ReDoS risk: the `setting` value is passed directly into `Regexp.new` without sanitization, so malicious settings could cause catastrophic backtracking.
